summary: Post-repair NVMe reports zero P-states causing prolonged low-power CPU state and AAD/Intune registration failures
description: Issue summary: Several recently returned/repaired laptops (Dell Precision 5560 and Latitude 7440) fail to complete Azure AD / Intune registration after SSD/NVMe replacement. Machines boot to Windows but provisioning times out during MDM enrollment and AAD device attestation. Impact: Blocking users from being re-enrolled after depot repairs; affects onboarding and turnaround times for depot returns. Environment: Production fleet, post-depot-repair images using standard corporate Task Sequence (SCCM/WinPE) and the latest post-image drivers. Reproducible on devices that had third-party NVMe firmware applied during depot repair.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replace NVMe SSD during depot repair; 2) Re-image device with standard corporate image (Win10/11 baseline) and drivers; 3) Boot and connect to corp network; 4) OOBE/Autopilot flow triggers AAD join and Intune MDM enrollment; 5) Enrollment times out or fails with TPM/attestation errors and device remains not-enrolled in Intune.
logs:
- Windows event log: DeviceEnrollmentManager timeout entries (DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider) timestamp 2026-03-05 09:12:23
- System log: Kernel reported ACPI CPPC reporting 0 performance states for CPU (Event ID custom telemetry) during early boot
- Imaging agent logs: nvme-identify returned firmware quirks flagged 'PSTATES_ZERO'
- Endpoint logs: TPM attestation retry count exceeded; 0x801c0001 timeouts
- Relevant sample device IDs: SN:DP5560-0123, SN:DL7440-0456
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed pattern only on devices that had NVMe replacements performed by third-party depot partner between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-04.
Hypothesis 1 (Hardware): Third-party NVMe firmware misreports NVMe identify fields leading Windows ACPI subsystem to mis-evaluate CPU P-state capability indirectly through OEM driver interaction.

Hypothesis 2 (OS/Driver): Our NVMe driver or power management shim sees a malformed identify and disables ACPI CPPC table parsing, causing scheduler to prefer deep low-power state; TPM attestation window is missed due to CPU being pinned to low performance.
Kernel debug: Reproduced with local lab unit. 'nvme id-ctrl' returned valid model but Capability bits cleared; a vendor-specific firmware quirk bit matches known vendor X pattern.
Cross-team signal: Hardware depot confirmed applying firmware bundle v3.2.1 from vendor X during staging; rollback to OEM firmware v2.9 resolved pstate reporting on a test unit.
Imaging script note: imaging-scripts currently do not validate NVMe controller identify flags post-replacement. Add validation step to detect vendor-quirk bit.
Related telemetry: Increase in post-repair intune enrollment failures from baseline 0.3% to 6.1% for affected models in us-west during window.
Temporary mitigation trial: Added a post-boot powerprofile change to High Performance as a workaround which allowed enrollment to complete in 3/3 lab re-tests.

resolution_notes: Root cause: Third-party depot-applied NVMe firmware v3.2.1 sets a vendor quirk that results in NVMe identify capability bits cleared. Interaction between NVMe controller behavior and OEM power management caused CPU performance states to be effectively unavailable during early boot, leading to prolonged low-power scheduling and windowed TPM/AAD attestation timeouts. Fixes implemented: 1) Imaging hotfix: imaging-scripts PR #298 adds a post-image NVMe validation step and sets temporary High Performance power plan for first boot to ensure attestation window; 2) Depot action: halted vendor X firmware bundle, initiated rollback on quarantined units; 3) Hardware team engaged vendor for firmware patch. Follow-ups: Add CI check in depot SOP to verify NVMe identify fields after any firmware writes, update post-repair validation runbook on Confluence, and monitor enrollment failure metric for the next 7 days.
follow_up_actions: Deploy imaging-scripts hotfix to all depots (PR merged 2026-03-08).
Vendor firmware patch expected ETA 2026-03-12; verify and validate before redeploy.
Add NVMe identify validation to Post-Repair Validation Checklist on Confluence.
Monitor FD enroller failures metric (metric id: ENROLL_FAIL_RATE) daily for 7 days and report to support leadership.
Schedule a retro with depot partner to prevent future uncoordinated firmware bundles.
